card.name: Shad Suk Mynsiem
card.tagline: Khasi 'Dance of the Joyful Heart' welcoming spring
card.profile: Ka Shad Suk Mynsiem ('Dance of the Joyful Heart/Souls') is a three-day Khasi thanksgiving spring festival held in April, marking the end of the harvest and the sowing of new seeds (Meghalaya House Delhi; Auchitya). Organised by the Seng Khasi, it centres on the historic Weiking Ground at Jaiaw, Shillong; unmarried maidens dance in an inner circle holding a white handkerchief symbolising maidenhood, while men dance vigorously around them with a sword in the right hand and a white yak-hair whisk in the left, to the beat of drums and the tangmuri pipes (Shillong Online; Sentinel Assam). The dance formation - women flanked and protected by men - reflects Meghalaya's matrilineal society (Scale Indigo).
card.insight: The first official Shad Suk Mynsiem dance was held on 14-15 April 1911 at Madan Weiking, Mawkhar, Shillong, and was formally given the name 'Ka Shad Suk Mynsiem' in 1912; the 2026 (115th) edition concluded in April 2026 with over a thousand dancers (The Shillong Times; Sentinel Assam).
